criteria.why: All formulas and numbers reproduce within <0.01%; assumptions (k=1.30, A_eff=320 mm2, beta=0.093) and prompt contradictions (:152/:160, E_crit) are disclosed with sensitivity analysis. Deducted 1.0 for two unjustified simplifications: (1) 96 mm paper cones credited with a full 96 mm crush stroke to zero residual thickness, though :243 admits ~20-25% densification at the end of travel; (2) the 60 mm free suspension stroke and the 96 mm cone crush are merged into one uniform deceleration of the whole M=0.458 kg at F_avg=276.8 N without matching the forces of the two stages (only the 105 g cradle decelerates over the first 60 mm; when the 105 g cradle hits the cone block with its 276.8 N crush threshold, the egg's own g-load would exceed 200 g).

Independent recomputation: total mass 398+60=458.0 g <= 500 g; sides 250x250x290 mm <= 300 mm; volume 0.018125 m3 <= 0.02 m3; cost $3.11 <= $5.00; build 28 min <= 30 min; 12 materials all allowed; film thickness 0.09 and 0.05 mm <= 2 mm; no glue/metal/glass/ready absorbers; egg fixed by suspension, not glued.

P1=0.943 decomposed by landing orientation; P3=0.730 (0.824 with block replacement) from a justified dependent-damage model with weak points and failure modes. But the key P(bottom)=0.96 rests on a 'low centre of mass' claim (:311) while the dimension chain (:78-82) puts the 105 g cradle at 177-232 mm from the floor in a 290 mm box, raising the tumble risk onto the side (152 g) or top (290 g).

Each of the 12 materials is motivated by its mechanism (plastic crush of 16 paper cones, elastic-viscous rubber suspension, contact pressure spread by cotton and tray, foam and EPS corner dampers). For a 10.0 the quantitative link is missing: buckling force of one paper cone (~17.3 N at 3.4 g) and total stiffness of eight rubber bands 120x3x1 mm over 60-165 mm are not estimated.

Full material table with masses, prices and dimensions, attachment method, closed height (290 mm) and width (250 mm) chains, totals. Deducted 1.5 for three internal mismatches: cardboard qty 1 as 250x250x3 mm without the 290 mm side walls and cap; five foam pads listed while a sixth 18 mm bottom pad is used in the scheme (:27), height chain (:81) and protection.bottom (:138); cradle width 52 mm in the width chain (:84-88) vs 140x120x40 and 140x140x40 blanks and the 56-60 mm longitudinal egg size at the declared transverse orientation (:282).

Concrete post-test plan with numbers (two-stage block 30+66 mm, k 1.30 -> 1.15, peak 80.1 -> 70.9 g; proof that a symmetric top stroke of 100 mm is impossible: 364 mm > 300 mm and 515 g > 500 g) and a full 20 m recomputation (v=19.81 m/s, t_f=2.02 s, Ek=89.86 J, d_min(100 g)=200 mm, peak 159 g, chain 334 mm > 300 mm).

section7_evidence: All five §7 conditions clean: (a) mass 458.0 g <= 500 g, sides 250x250x290 mm <= 300 mm, volume 0.018125 m3 <= 0.02 m3, cost $3.11 <= $5.00, build 28 min; (b) full calculations present and verified; (c) six directions protected with nonzero stroke; (d) egg suspended on 8 rubber bands over a replaceable 16-cone crush block, not rigid to the shell; (e) only allowed materials, film <= 2 mm, no glue/metal/glass/ready absorbers.
